why: All three checks pass. (1) Quote is VERBATIM. curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary.md line 45 (section '### Auto memory') reads in full: 'Notes Claude writes for itself based on your corrections and preferences, stored per git repository under `~/.claude/projects/`. All worktrees of the same repository share one auto memory directory. The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the `MEMORY.md` index loads at the start of every session. Auto memory is the Claude-written counterpart to [CLAUDE.md](#claude-md), which you write.' Nothing later in the line reverses it. memory.md:384 states the same rule with more force ('Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start') and memory.md:390 scopes it ('This limit applies only to `MEMORY.md`. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length'), so the byte cap is a MEMORY.md-specific rule, not a general instruction-file rule. (2) Cited file:line is accurate. packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 is `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and :29-32 is `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT)` doing `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` with no byte check. `grep -rna` (with -a, so NUL-byte files are not skipped) over packages/shared/src/agent/memory finds only AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256*1024 in memory-cleanup.ts (the scheduled rewrite pass's input guard, not a load cap) and RULE_PATTERN_EXPANSION_BYTE_LIMIT = 4MB in rule-matching.ts (glob expansion). No 25 KB constant exists anywhere in the memory subsystem. (3) Consequence verified separately, one layer up and one layer down, and it is WORSE than claimed rather than refuted. Layer down: readMemoryFile's two call sites are prompts/system.ts:455 (via loadMemoryPromptBlock) and capabilities/native-sources.ts:427 (an @import-discovery line scan, not a content load). Layer up: system.ts:453-455 reads `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`, so the 200-line route is the LEGACY fallback only — AGENTS.md already records that the capability runtime is active on every normal send. The live route is: buildNativeCapabilityInventory registers `join(configDir,'MEMORY.md')` (and the session MEMORY.md) as `kind:'memory'` records via memoryFileRecords (native-sources.ts:909-916, :980-989); views.ts:218-219 puts them in `view.memory` with no size filter; base-agent.ts composePinnedCapabilityContext iterates `runtime.view.memory` and calls `runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)`; materializer.ts:169-185 does `readFileSync(contentPath)` and returns `content.toString('utf-8')` whole. The content is pushed verbatim into the pinned block that rides every session. So on the shipped path neither the 25 KB byte cap nor even the 200-line cap applies. Not a recorded owner decision: inert-worklist section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touch memory loading. Not a deliberate fork difference either: this is not a Claude/ChatGPT subscription flow, not gateway-specific, and not a rename. The parity audit at :1672-1675 independently names 'a documented load limit (first 200 lines or 25 KB of `MEMORY.md`, whichever comes first, with frontmatter and HTML comments stripped before measurement)' as part of the auto-memory subsystem it found we had understated. The only inaccuracy in the finding is its mechanism sentence 'we cap only lines' — true of the legacy composer, false of the live one, which caps nothing.
correctedState: There is no 25 KB byte cap on the MEMORY.md load anywhere in the repo (memory-store.ts:8 declares only MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200; the only byte constants in packages/shared/src/agent/memory are AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256 KB for the cleanup rewrite pass and RULE_PATTERN_EXPANSION_BYTE_LIMIT = 4 MB for glob expansion). The gap is broader than the finding states: the 200-line cap in readMemoryFile (memory-store.ts:29-32) governs only the LEGACY composer, which prompts/system.ts:453-455 skips whenever the capability runtime is pinned — i.e. on every normal send — plus an @import-discovery line scan at native-sources.ts:427. On the live route the global ~/.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md and the session MEMORY.md are registered as kind:'memory' capability records (native-sources.ts:909-916, :980-989), carried unfiltered into view.memory (views.ts:218-219), and read by materializer.readText (materializer.ts:169-185), which readFileSync's the whole file and returns it; base-agent.ts composePinnedCapabilityContext pushes that verbatim into the pinned block. So MEMORY.md enters every session's context with NEITHER a byte cap NOR a line cap. Also missing, per memory.md:384-386: the pre-measurement stripping of frontmatter and HTML comments, and the post-write over-limit error (tracked separately as f166). memory.md:390 confirms the cap is MEMORY.md-specific and must not be applied to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instruction layers, which are correctly loaded in full.
